source.title: Beyond Binary Rewards: A Comparative Study of Reward Design for Reinforcement Unlearning
source.authors: Efstratios Zaradoukas; Davide Gabrielli; Bardh Prenkaj; Gjergji Kasneci

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests unlearning performance with a different reward-design method and includes adversarial-attack probes, but does not test recovery by fine-tuning, activation edits, or quantization.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for forget-set probes, including an aggregate adversarial-attack (AA) split, and utility benchmarks. It does not report attack results separately by attack type or compare attacked and un-attacked prompts on the same unlearned model. Statements about the methods being faster, and reward values used to configure them, are not separate findings about the claim.
record.test_reason: This is a new RL-based unlearning method (PURGE-style GRPO rewards) evaluated on RWKU with Phi-3-Mini. Its forget, adversarial-probe and utility results bear on Version A: whether unlearning reaches near-chance recall, keeps ability, and resists simple attacks. It runs no relearning, activation-ablation or quantization attacks. It makes no robustness claim against such attacks, so Version F is not tested. Its AA probes are aggregated and not compared with unattacked probes on the same facts, so they cannot show recovery by prompting (Version E).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right: denser rewards (exponential, PageRank) speed forgetting, and PageRank-Softmax reaches Binary's step-1500 forgetting by step 500 with utility kept. One correction: at step 1500, Exponential is slightly worse than Binary on all forget metrics (FB 0.379 vs 0.372, QA 0.382 vs 0.365, AA 0.417 vs 0.408). Only PageRank-Softmax beats Binary. The authors also say neighboring knowledge is not degraded, although Neighbor FB falls for all methods.
record.recipe_differences: Builds on PURGE and reproduces its binary-reward baseline, but compares new exponential and PageRank reward designs rather than testing recovery attacks such as relearning or weight edits.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that exponential-reward performance varies with τ and identifies τ = 0.5 as the best tested setting; PageRank weight redistribution also changes results, with PageRank Softmax outperforming the reported alternatives.
record.problems: Only Phi-3-Mini-4K-Instruct is tested. The study reports aggregated AA results rather than results for each attack type, and does not provide a chance-level reference or a direct attacked-versus-unattacked comparison.
record.rows_left_out: Neighbor, MIA, and training-step results are omitted because they do not directly measure the claim versions' targeted-knowledge recovery or utility conditions. Additional PageRank-variant results in Table 2 and Appendix D are not extracted because they compare reward variants rather than report a separate recovery attack outcome.

untested.parts: No chance-level reference for ROUGE-L recall. Only one model (Phi-3-Mini) and only RL-reward unlearning methods were tested.
No activation ablation or block-vs-delete analysis.
AA probes are aggregated over nine types, with no per-type results. There is no same-item attacked vs unattacked comparison, so recovery by prompting cannot be read.
The paper claims no robustness to recovery attacks; it reports only standard RWKU AA probes.

missing.what: Neighbor FB drops from 0.604 to 0.456-0.474 for all rewards (Neighbor QA from 0.537 to ~0.50). This is collateral loss of adjacent knowledge, relevant to A's preservation clause.
Forget FB/QA/AA at convergence across the tau sweep: weak forgetting at tau=0.1, best at 0.5. The forgetting level depends on reward hyperparameters.
Forget and AA scores for other PageRank variants. For example, PR-Argmax has Forget FB 0.467 and AA 0.444, showing strong method dependence.

record.verdict_notes: This is a method-efficiency paper, not a robustness study. The record's F label is removed because the paper claims no resistance to recovery attacks. The E label is removed because AA results can't separate attack-driven recovery from residual knowledge: different item sets, no per-attack breakdown. Post-unlearning AA recall is above FB/QA recall for every method, but base AA is below base FB, so this hints that attacks retain more knowledge. The authors' 'at most 0.014' utility-shift statement is contradicted by TRU (-0.021) and FAC (+0.034). FLU Base and unlearned values appear to be on different scales.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not establish a chance-level reference for its forget metrics, nor does it test all unlearning methods named in the claim.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning set is tested.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of access-blocking versus deletion is tested.
No quantization of unlearned weights is tested.
The AA split aggregates nine probe types; the paper does not report individual attack types or compare attacks directly with ordinary prompts on the same unlearned checkpoint.
The paper tests aggregate AA probes, but not recovery by fine-tuning, activation edits, or quantization, and does not establish a direct attacked-versus-unattacked comparison.

relationships.condition: Phi-3-Mini-4K-Instruct on RWKU (20 targets, 1,500 steps); Binary, Exponential and PageRank-Softmax rewards
relationships.reason: Utility stays close to Base (GA/RA/TRU/FAC rows). However, forget recall drops only ~32-47% (FB/QA rows), and attack probes keep 0.39-0.42 recall, above plain probes (AA rows). Forgetting is far from near-chance.
relationships.display_finding: Utility stayed near baseline, but forget recall declined only about 32–47%, and attack probes retained 0.39–0.42 recall, exceeding plain probes.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Forget scores fall relative to Base and utility scores remain close, but the paper gives no chance reference, so near-chance targeted accuracy is not established; see FB-Binary, FB-Exp, FB-PR, QA-Binary, QA-Exp, QA-PR, and the utility rows.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Aggregate RWKU AA probes across the tested reward methods
reader_labels.reason: Attack-probe scores are below Base but remain nonzero, and the aggregate results do not show whether attacks recover more than ordinary prompts on the same unlearned model; see AA-Binary, AA-Exp, and AA-PR.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: PageRank Softmax, Exponential Decay, and PURGE Binary on aggregate AA probes
reader_labels.reason: The methods reduce AA scores relative to Base, but the study reports residual AA recall and does not directly compare attacked with un-attacked prompting or test the other attack types separately; see AA-Binary, AA-Exp, and AA-PR.
